name: Revenue recognition — sale of goods
definition: Revenue from a sale of goods is recognised when performance is achieved: the seller has transferred the property in the goods, or all significant risks and rewards of ownership, and retains no effective control; and no significant uncertainty exists about the amount of consideration.
why_it_exists: Fixes WHEN a sale enters the books. Recognising too early overstates profit for the period; too late understates it. The trigger is transfer of risk and reward, not the invoice date and not the payment date.
inputs: evidence of transfer of property or of risks and rewards
evidence of retained control, if any
preconditions: a sale-of-goods transaction, not a service
exceptions: UNKNOWN — AS-9 scope exclusions not yet extracted
common_mistakes: recognising on invoice date when risks and rewards have not transferred
recognising on payment receipt, which is a cash-basis error
ignoring retained effective control, which defeats transfer
legal_references: UNKNOWN — statutory backing via Companies Act s.129 not yet extracted
gst_references: NOT APPLICABLE — GST time of supply is a separate determination and must not be conflated with accounting revenue recognition
evidence_required: document evidencing transfer of property or risk
confidence_factors: weak when delivery terms are absent from the document
weak when the document does not show whether control was retained
validation_checks: recognition date is not before the transfer of risks and rewards
consideration amount is certain, or recognition is postponed
examples: goods delivered, title passed, price agreed, no return right retained — recognise
counterexamples: goods shipped on sale-or-return with unexpired return right — significant risks not transferred

evidence.quote: the seller of goods has transferred to the buyer the property in the goods for a price
evidence.extraction_note: The span continuing 'or allsignificant risks and rewards' is quoted separately: the PDF extraction joins 'all' and 'significant'. The artifact is in the extraction, not in the standard.

evidence.quote: the seller retains no effective control of the goods transferred to a degree usually associated with ownership
no significant uncertainty exists regarding the amount of the consideration that will be derived from the sale of the goods
